jobs.title: Territory Manager – Point of Care Ultrasound (POCUS)
jobs.description: Location: Northern England (ideally based in Manchester, Leeds or Liverpool) Salary: £40,000 - £50,000 basic + £24,000 target bonus with uncapped earning potential Benefits: Tesla company car, 25 days' holiday, pension, life assurance and comprehensive benefits package Who You Will Be Working For You will be joining an established healthcare solutions provider supplying innovative medical technologies to hospitals and healthcare professionals. Following an exciting new distributor partnership, the company is building a dedicated UK sales team to support the growth of its Point of Care Ultrasound (POCUS) portfolio. This is an opportunity to join a new team at an early stage, introducing award-winning ultrasound technology to healthcare professionals and helping to establish its presence across the UK market. Why Should You Join? Brand-new team: Join a newly established sales team and play a key role in developing the POCUS business across Northern England. Exciting technology: Represent an award-winning ultrasound product in a growing area of medical technology. Excellent earning potential: £24,000 annual target bonus, paid quarterly, with uncapped commission and additional earnings for exceeding target. Autonomy and ownership: Take responsibility for developing your territory, identifying new opportunities and building lasting customer relationships. Attractive package: Tesla company car, generous annual leave, enhanced pension, life assurance and a wide range of employee benefits. Working with healthcare professionals across Urology, Critical Care, Intensive Care, Anaesthetics, Emergency Medicine and Vascular Access, you will introduce the technology, demonstrate its clinical benefits and develop new business opportunities. Proactively identifying and securing new business opportunities across NHS hospitals and healthcare organisations. Building relationships with stakeholders ranging from nurses and consultants to departmental managers, clinical engineering, medical physics and procurement teams. Delivering product demonstrations, presentations and clinical education to support adoption of POCUS technology. Managing the sales process from initial prospecting and customer engagement through to negotiation and closing. Working with the Field Sales Manager to identify opportunities for Trust-wide and ICB-wide software sales. Developing relationships with key opinion leaders and clinical decision-makers. Supporting clinical workshops, study days, exhibitions and product launches. Monitoring competitor activity and identifying opportunities to increase market share. Collaborating with colleagues across the wider business to maximise opportunities and deliver excellent customer service. What You Will Need We are looking for an energetic, commercially driven individual who enjoys developing new business and has the determination to build a successful territory. Ideally, you will have: At least 12 months' experience selling medical devices or equipment into the NHS. A proven ability to identify opportunities, build relationships and close sales. Experience selling point of care technology, ultrasound or capital medical equipment would be advantageous. An understanding of NHS purchasing processes and the ability to engage with clinical and non-clinical decision-makers. Strong presentation, communication and negotiation skills. Alternatively, if you have a relevant clinical ultrasound background and are interested in moving into medical sales, please get in touch to discuss the opportunity.

jobs.title: Business Development Executive – Regulated Sectors
jobs.description: Location: Home-based, covering a national UK territory Products and services: Temperature and humidity monitoring systems, UKAS-accredited calibration, temperature mapping and validation Customers: Medical, healthcare, pharmaceutical, laboratory, warehousing and cold-chain distribution organisations Who you'll be working for Tek-Troniks is a privately owned British manufacturer with over 30 years’ experience in temperature and humidity monitoring, calibration and validation. Its products and services help customers protect temperature-sensitive materials, maintain accurate records and demonstrate regulatory compliance. The company designs and manufactures its products in the UK, combining established technical capabilities with the accessible management structure of a small business. It already supplies regulated organisations, including NHS customers, pharmaceutical businesses and distribution facilities, and is now appointing a dedicated national salesperson to develop these markets. Why should you join? Freedom to manage your territory: You’ll decide where to focus your efforts and when customer visits, demonstrations or remote meetings will best move an opportunity forward. Performance is measured through commercial results, with no prescribed weekly field-visit target. An established proposition with room to grow: You’ll represent proven products and services in markets where the company already has customers, with considerable scope to develop new relationships and opportunities. Uncapped earning potential: The commission scheme rewards both new business and qualifying repeat revenue from accounts you originate, allowing you to benefit from the relationships you build. A voice in the business: Working closely with senior management, you’ll help shape market priorities, sales processes and marketing activity, while feeding customer insight into future product development. Technical support and training: You’ll learn from the General Manager and work directly with colleagues in engineering, calibration, internal sales and production. What the role involves You’ll take ownership of new business development across the UK, selling an integrated range of monitoring systems, calibration and mapping services into regulated environments. This is a consultative sales role, helping customers understand how the company’s solutions can meet their operational and compliance requirements. Your responsibilities will include: Identifying and approaching prospective customers across healthcare, pharmaceuticals, laboratories and regulated distribution. Building relationships with technical, quality, compliance and purchasing stakeholders. Understanding customer requirements, arranging demonstrations and preparing appropriate proposals and quotations. Managing opportunities from initial enquiry through to negotiation and sale. Developing accounts beyond the first installation, including opportunities across additional sites. Assessing relevant public-sector tenders and other routes to market. Maintaining a sustainable pipeline and contributing ideas to the company’s commercial approach. You’ll work from home, travelling nationally when required, with occasional overnight stays. Initial training will include approximately three to four weeks working closely with the business to develop your product and market knowledge. Person requirements You’ll have proven technical or consultative sales experience within a regulated market, together with evidence of winning new business and managing opportunities through to completion. Your background could include medical or pharmaceutical equipment, laboratory instrumentation, environmental monitoring, calibration, validation, cold-chain technology, aseptic processing or sterile services. Direct temperature monitoring experience isn’t essential if you bring relevant sector knowledge and the ability to learn a technical portfolio. You’ll also need: An understanding of quality systems, documented processes and the expectations of regulated customers. The confidence to discuss technical requirements and build credibility with specialist decision-makers. Strong prospecting, relationship-building and commercial skills. The judgement and self-motivation to manage a national territory independently. A willingness to learn, ask questions and contribute ideas as the business develops. Knowledge of GxP, MHRA or GDP requirements would be valuable. An existing network of quality or compliance contacts would also be an advantage. Basic salary: Circa £50,000–£60,000 Bonus: Uncapped commission, with £18,000 commission at the annual revenue target, plus qualifying trailing commission Car allowance: £5,000 per annum

jobs.title: UK Clinical Specialist - Spinal Robotics
jobs.description: Location: National, field-based role covering the UK Products: Spinal surgical robotics and navigation technology Who you’ll be working for: Our client is a global medical technology company with an established reputation in orthopaedics and spinal surgery. Its portfolio includes surgical implants, instruments and digital technologies that support healthcare professionals in delivering patient care. The UK spine business is expanding, with new systems joining its portfolio and a spinal robotics platform preparing for introduction to the UK market. Why should you join? You’ll join a world-leading medical technology company with a reputation for excellence at a significant stage in the growth of its UK spine business. The portfolio is expanding with new spinal deformity systems launching, alongside the first UK introduction of its spinal robot at the end of the year. This gives you the opportunity to play a central role in introducing the technology to hospitals, supporting surgeons and theatre teams from their first cases through to confident, routine use. You’ll work in an environment that supports your career aspirations and promotes your physical and mental wellbeing. Alongside a competitive salary and bonus, you’ll receive a comprehensive benefits package with options you can tailor to what matters to you at different stages of your life. Job overview As Clinical Specialist, you’ll lead the clinical introduction, adoption and effective use of spinal robotics and navigation technology across UK hospitals. You’ll act as the clinical expert for surgeons and hospital teams, helping them integrate the technology into their surgical workflows and use it safely and consistently. Working closely with sales, marketing and medical education colleagues, you’ll support new site launches, deliver training and provide practical support in theatre. The position involves significant travel across the UK and requires someone comfortable working independently. Your responsibilities will include: Leading clinical implementation and supporting the launch of systems into new centres. Providing in-theatre case support and troubleshooting clinical and technical issues. Delivering hands-on training, product demonstrations and structured education for surgeons and theatre teams. Supporting case planning, surgical workflows and consistent use of the technology. Building relationships with spinal surgeons, nursing teams, hospital management and digital stakeholders. Encouraging sustained utilisation and monitoring clinical usage, performance and outcomes. Supporting evaluations, bids and account plans alongside the wider commercial team. Sharing customer feedback and clinical insights to inform product and workflow improvements. Your requirements Experience with robotics in spinal surgery is essential for this position. You’ll bring a strong understanding of spinal procedures and the operating theatre environment, together with the confidence to support surgical teams during live cases. We’re looking for: A clinical background, such as an ODP, scrub nurse, allied health professional or equivalent. Relevant experience in spinal surgery, orthopaedics and enabling technologies, including spinal robotics. A thorough understanding of surgical workflows and the practical demands of theatre. Strong communication, presentation and training skills, with the ability to explain technical information clearly. The ability to build credibility with surgeons and work effectively with multidisciplinary hospital teams. A practical approach to troubleshooting and supporting the adoption of new technology. The organisation and independence needed to manage a national, field-based role with significant travel. Basic salary: £52,000 to £61,000 Bonus: £18,000 per annum, paid quarterly Car: Company car with electric and hybrid options, or allowance options of £7,000 cash or £6,000 towards a lease per year Benefits: 25 days’ holiday, pension, healthcare, lunch allowance, laptop and a range of flexible benefits and employee discounts

jobs.title: Territory Manager - Ambulance & Post-Acute Care
jobs.description: Location: Ideally based in the South West or South Wales. The territory covers the South West, South Wales and West Midlands up to Birmingham, plus Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire, Berkshire, Hampshire and Surrey. Products: You’ll sell a focused portfolio of medical devices across ambulance, acute and community care settings: Falls recovery equipment: An established lifting chair that helps people recover safely from the floor following a fall. Customers include ambulance services, care home groups, occupational therapists and NHS manual handling teams. Non-contact thermometers: A newly introduced range listed on NHS Supply Chain and HCA frameworks, with opportunities across acute wards, paediatrics, oncology and critical care. Key contacts include clinical leads, infection control teams, clinical engineering and procurement. The role combines developing an established customer base for falls recovery equipment with winning new business for the temperature monitoring range. The company Our client is an established medical device distributor working with leading healthcare manufacturers across the UK and Ireland. Combining specialist sales expertise with clinical education and technical support, the business helps healthcare professionals introduce and use technologies that improve patient care. You’ll join its ambulance and post-acute care division, supplying practical solutions to NHS Trusts, ambulance services, care homes and community healthcare teams. With an established customer base and a newly launched product range, this is an opportunity to build on existing relationships while developing new business within a close, supportive team. Why you should join You’ll take responsibility for a growing territory with an established customer base and a newly launched product range. This gives you the opportunity to develop existing accounts while building new business across hospitals, ambulance services and care providers. The products have a practical impact on patient care, helping people recover safely after falls and supporting clinical teams with temperature monitoring. You’ll join a close, supportive team with the independence to plan your territory and take ownership of its growth. Responsibilities Grow sales, revenue and market share across the territory, achieving agreed sales and margin targets. Develop existing accounts for an established falls recovery product and win new customers for a recently launched non-contact thermometer. Build relationships with ambulance services, NHS Trusts, care home groups and community healthcare providers. Engage clinical and commercial decision-makers, including procurement, infection prevention and control, manual handling teams, occupational therapists, paramedics and clinical engineering departments. Deliver practical product demonstrations, customer training and assessments, including in patients’ homes where required. Support product evaluations and work with customers through procurement and approval processes. Maintain a territory business plan, manage your pipeline and keep customer records and sales forecasts up to date. Attend exhibitions, workshops, training and supplier meetings, including occasional overseas travel and weekend commitments. Person requirements You’ll be a self-motivated sales professional who enjoys finding opportunities, opening doors and converting interest into business. You’ll be comfortable managing a broad territory independently, while contributing to a supportive team. Ideally, you’ll bring experience selling medical devices or consumables into NHS Trusts or community services, with an understanding of NHS procurement, clinical evaluations and purchasing approvals. Driven candidates with relevant transferable sales experience will also be considered. You’ll need: Strong relationship-building, presentation and negotiation skills. The drive to win new business alongside the discipline to develop existing accounts. A warm, sensitive approach when working with vulnerable patients and their families. The ability to transport equipment and carry out practical product demonstrations safely. Good organisation, IT skills and a full driving licence. Willingness to travel throughout the territory and undertake the required DBS checks. Experience selling into ambulance services or care homes would be an advantage, as would knowledge of NHS Wales procurement and health boards. A clinical background in nursing, paramedicine or occupational therapy would also be valuable. Basic salary: £35,000 to £46,000 per annum. Bonus: £24,000 per annum, paid quarterly, combining a target-based bonus with uncapped commission, currently 2% on sales. Company car: Tesla. You’ll also receive: 25 days’ annual leave, increasing with service after five years to a maximum of 30 days. 5% employer pension contribution. Life assurance worth four times your annual salary. Permanent health insurance to support you if you’re unable to work due to illness or injury. Enhanced family leave and sick pay. Confidential 24/7 employee assistance programme for you and your household, plus access to trained Mental Health First Aiders. Funded eye tests, a contribution towards eyewear and a Cycle to Work scheme. Volunteer days, charity sponsorship support, employee events and recognition awards. Access to financial advice, retirement planning support and an employee savings scheme. £5/day lunch allowance

jobs.title: Inside Sales Executive
jobs.description: Location: Sheffield, predominantly office-based Products: Breast Care, Orthotics and Walking Aids Who you will be working for Our client is a well-established global manufacturer and distributor of healthcare products, specialising in breast care, orthotics and walking aids. Their products support patients' mobility, independence and quality of life, with customers including the NHS, private healthcare providers, specialist clinics and distributors. Due to continued growth, they are looking to recruit an Inside Sales Executive to join their Sheffield-based team, supporting sales activity across the UK. Why you should join Join an established, successful healthcare company with a strong reputation and excellent staff retention. Become part of a close-knit, friendly and supportive team where people genuinely enjoy working together. Work with an approachable manager who encourages independence, trusts her team and doesn't micromanage. Enjoy a varied role combining sales, account management, business development and market research. Receive full product training, so previous medical device or healthcare experience isn't essential. Have the opportunity to develop your commercial skills and potentially progress into a field-based sales role. Join a growing team where you can take ownership of your work and make a genuine contribution to business growth. Job responsibilities This is a varied, office-based sales position combining existing account management, proactive new business development and support for the external sales team. You will work across three product groups, breast care, orthotics and walking aids, helping to identify and develop opportunities throughout the UK. Your responsibilities will include: Proactively identifying and developing new business opportunities through telephone, email and digital engagement. Managing and developing relationships with existing customers, including NHS departments, private healthcare providers, clinics and distributors. Researching potential customers, mapping market opportunities and identifying areas for business growth. Following up sales leads, customer enquiries and marketing campaigns to convert opportunities into orders. Identifying cross-selling and upselling opportunities across the product portfolio. Supporting the external Territory Managers with prospecting, customer appointments and regional sales development. Preparing and following up quotations, pricing proposals and tender documentation. Maintaining and updating customer databases, ensuring accurate contact information and sales records. Assisting with product launches, training activities, promotional campaigns and events. Monitoring sales opportunities, tracking progress against targets and providing market and competitor intelligence. Working closely with customer service, marketing and operations to ensure customers receive a professional and responsive service. Person requirements We are looking for a proactive, commercially minded individual who enjoys speaking with customers, developing relationships and finding new business opportunities. This role would particularly suit someone in the early stages of their sales career who is keen to take on more responsibility and develop within the healthcare industry. Essential: Previous experience in an internal sales, telesales, outbound sales or customer-facing sales role, ideally with at least 1-2 years' experience. Confident telephone manner with the ability to build rapport and develop customer relationships. A proactive approach to prospecting and identifying new sales opportunities. Strong communication, organisational and administrative skills. Self-motivated, resilient and comfortable working towards sales targets. Able to work independently, use initiative and manage competing priorities. Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and Excel. Adaptable and comfortable working across different products, customers and sales approaches. Desirable: Experience within healthcare, medical devices or a related industry. Knowledge of NHS customers, procurement or tender processes. Experience preparing quotations or supporting field-based sales teams. Previous healthcare experience is not essential. More important is your enthusiasm for sales, willingness to learn and ability to take ownership of opportunities. Salary and benefits Basic salary: £27,000 - £30,000 Bonus potential: £6,000 Annual leave: 24 days plus bank holidays Pension: Company pension scheme Location: Sheffield, predominantly office-based with occasional customer travel Training: Full product training and ongoing development Career progression: Potential opportunity to move into an external sales position

jobs.title: Territory Sales Manager - Airway Management & Visualisation
jobs.description: Location: Sussex, Kent, Surrey, Hampshire & the South Coast including Dartford, Medway, Canterbury, Tunbridge, Brighton, Portsmouth, Southampton, Reading, Guildford, Redhill. You'll need to live within or close to the territory and be comfortable travelling regularly to customer sites. Products: Video laryngoscopy, bronchoscopy and airway management systems Who you'll be working for A global medical device manufacturer and recognised market leader in video laryngoscopy, providing innovative technologies that help clinicians improve patient care. The company specialises in advanced visualisation and airway management solutions, including video laryngoscopes and single-use bronchoscopes used across critical care, anaesthesia and operating theatres. With an established reputation, a growing respiratory and pulmonology portfolio and a strong commitment to product innovation, the business offers an exciting opportunity to join a successful and expanding team. Why should you join? Market-leading products: Represent the global market leader in video laryngoscopy, with an established customer base and a growing portfolio of airway management solutions. Excellent earning potential: Uncapped monthly commission with accelerators once you exceed target, providing genuine opportunities to increase your earnings. Career development: Comprehensive product training, ongoing professional development and opportunities for internal progression. Supportive team culture: Join a close-knit, collaborative team that regularly gets together for company events, celebrations and team-building activities. Employee wellbeing: A company that values work-life balance, employee engagement and wellbeing, with a comprehensive benefits package. The role As Territory Sales Manager, you'll take responsibility for developing and growing sales of a market-leading range of video laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy systems across the South East. This is a customer-facing role combining new business development with account management. You'll work closely with clinicians and hospital decision-makers, demonstrating how the company's technology can improve clinical workflows and patient care. Your responsibilities will include: Managing and developing an established territory, identifying opportunities to grow existing accounts and win new business. Building strong relationships with anaesthetists, surgeons, theatre teams, critical care clinicians, nursing staff and senior hospital decision-makers. Conducting product demonstrations, evaluations and presentations to demonstrate the clinical and commercial benefits of the portfolio. Identifying new business opportunities through proactive prospecting and regular face-to-face customer engagement. Managing the full sales process, from initial engagement and product evaluation through to proposals, negotiations and closing sales. Developing territory business plans, maintaining an accurate sales pipeline and working towards monthly, quarterly and annual targets. Working with clinical and commercial stakeholders to understand their challenges and provide appropriate solutions. Who we're looking for We're looking for a driven, ambitious and commercially minded individual who enjoys being out in front of customers and has the motivation to develop new business. You don't need previous airway management experience, as comprehensive product training will be provided. Ideally, you'll bring: Some field sales experience, preferably within medical devices, healthcare or another B2B environment. Experience selling into operating theatres, anaesthesia or critical care would be advantageous, but isn't essential. An understanding of capital equipment sales or experience managing product evaluations would be beneficial. Confidence building relationships with clinical and commercial decision-makers. A proactive, competitive approach to sales, with the resilience and determination to pursue new opportunities. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage your own territory, priorities and sales pipeline. Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence customers at different levels. We're also interested in hearing from people earlier in their sales careers , including Associate Sales Representatives who are ready to take on their own territory. If you're a self-starter with the drive to succeed, the company is willing to invest in your development. Salary & Benefits Basic salary: £45,000–£58,000 depending on experience. Bonus: Uncapped commission based on sales, paid monthly, with accelerators above 100% of target. Company car or car allowance: £650 per month (£7,800 annually). Pension: 4% employer contribution with 5% employee contribution through salary sacrifice. Private healthcare: AXA. Health cash plan: Simplyhealth, providing support towards dental, GP, chiropractic and other healthcare costs. Additional benefits: Paid leave, family and medical leave provisions, employee wellbeing initiatives and professional development opportunities.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager – Orthopaedic Power Tools

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager – Middle East & Africa
jobs.description: Location: UK-based, home working with extensive international travel across the Middle East and Africa. Territory excludes South Africa and Israel. To be based ideally within one hour of Aylesbury, however, they are flexible for the right person with good access to a major international airport. Product: Premium surgical power tools and associated technology used across orthopaedic and other bone surgery applications. Who you’ll be working for: A privately owned, family-run medical device manufacturer with a global presence and more than a century of heritage. This is a newly created position resulting from continued growth within the international business. You’ll inherit an established region generating approximately £2.3m in annual sales, with existing distributor relationships, account history and internal knowledge already in place. The company has a strong reputation for product quality, responsive customer service and long-term relationships. Long service is common, and people are given considerable autonomy once trust has been established. What you’ll enjoy: Taking ownership of an established multimillion-pound international region rather than starting with a blank sheet of paper. A clear growth opportunity, with a target of approximately £2.7m compared with £2.3m in sales during the previous year. Developing sales through an established network of distributors and agents across a diverse range of international markets. Considerable autonomy over your diary, travel and commercial priorities. Working for a privately owned business with a long-term approach to growth and product development. An uncapped commission scheme paid on actual sales, with no minimum threshold before you start earning commission. A structured handover from the experienced Regional Managers who currently manage these markets. What you’ll be doing: Managing and developing an existing network of distributors and agents across the Middle East and Africa. Identifying opportunities to increase market penetration and grow sales across the region. Assessing distributor performance and helping partners improve their product knowledge, sales capability and commercial activity. Identifying gaps in market coverage and, where necessary, evaluating, recruiting and onboarding new or replacement distributors. Supporting distributors with important opportunities, product demonstrations, trials and customer meetings. Building relationships with hospitals, surgeons and other end users alongside local partners. Managing capital equipment opportunities with sales cycles ranging from a matter of weeks to 6–12 months. Planning and undertaking international trips involving multiple countries, distributors and customer meetings. Preparing quotations, following up opportunities and maintaining momentum across the territory between visits. You should expect to tour the region approximately three to four times per year, with individual trips potentially lasting two to three weeks. Overall, you’re likely to spend around a quarter to a third of the year away from home. Here’s what you need: Medical device sales experience, ideally involving surgical or technically complex products. International sales or distributor/channel management experience would be advantageous, but isn't essential. Strong commercial drive and the ability to develop sales through other people. Excellent organisation and the ability to manage multiple countries, partners, opportunities and travel plans. The confidence and self-sufficiency to work independently from home and while travelling internationally. Sound commercial judgement and a calm, constructive approach when plans change or problems arise. The ability and willingness to develop sufficient technical and clinical knowledge to credibly support product demonstrations, trials and customer discussions. A genuine appetite for extensive international travel. Salary: Up to approximately £50,000, dependent on experience. Bonus: 1.2% commission on sales, paid monthly in arrears. No threshold and no commission cap. Indicative first-year OTE approximately £77,800–£82,800, dependent on territory sales performance. Car policy: £7,200 annual car allowance. Benefits: 25 days' holiday, 6% employer pension contribution, company-funded flights, accommodation and reasonable meals/expenses, company credit card for appropriate travel expenditure, travel insurance and time off in lieu for bank holidays spent travelling.

jobs.title: Territory Manager – Vascular
jobs.description: Location: Scotland. This is a field-based role covering Scotland, with key accounts and opportunities across Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Golden Jubilee, Edinburgh, Dundee, Grampian/Aberdeen and surrounding referral networks. Who you'll be working for : Our client is a global medical device company specialising in devices, implants and services for the treatment of peripheral vascular disease. The business operates internationally, with products sold in more than 90 countries. Its portfolio is focused primarily on the needs of vascular surgeons and includes products used across aortic, AV access, cardiac, carotid, lower extremity and neuro applications. Despite its global reach, the company deliberately maintains an entrepreneurial, small-company culture with an emphasis on teamwork, commercial freedom and decentralised decision-making. Why you should join : This is a role for someone who wants genuine ownership of their territory rather than operating within a heavily structured corporate sales environment. Scotland already has an established customer presence, but there is considerable headroom to grow product adoption, reactivate accounts and develop new business. You will have the freedom to identify where the opportunities lie and shape your territory accordingly. You will also have access to a broad specialist portfolio rather than being restricted to a single product, creating multiple opportunities to engage customers and develop accounts. The culture particularly suits commercially driven people who enjoy autonomy, are prepared to create their own opportunities and want their individual contribution to have a visible impact on business performance. The company combines the reach of an international medical device business with a more agile, entrepreneurial working environment. This is not simply an account maintenance role. You will be expected to actively create growth by understanding individual accounts, identifying gaps in product usage, developing clinical advocates and introducing products into new areas. What you'll need : You will ideally be an experienced medical device sales professional who is comfortable working within surgical, theatre or procedural environments. Willingness to travel extensively throughout Scotland. jobs.description: An exciting opportunity to join a global healthcare organisation with a long legacy of innovation in a high-growth commercial role. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced dental salesperson, orthodontic professional or clinically experienced candidate looking to develop their career into a territory-based commercial position. You’ll be representing a well-established portfolio across Dental and Orthodontics, working with dental professionals and key decision makers to develop existing accounts, identify new business opportunities and drive sustainable growth across your territory. Why this role stands out Join a global healthcare company with decades of innovation Manage an established territory across the North West, Midlands and South Yorkshire Represent a broad and clinically credible Dental & Orthodontic portfolio Develop existing customer relationships while identifying new business opportunities Work closely with dental and orthodontic professionals, supporting education and training Strong earning potential with uncapped bonus Company car and comprehensive benefits package Supportive, collaborative environment with genuine career progression Excellent opportunity for an ambitious dental/orthodontic professional to develop commercially The Company This organisation is a global healthcare leader known for delivering innovative, evidence-based solutions across healthcare and dental environments. jobs.title: Graduate Technical Sales Executive
jobs.description: Graduate Technical Engineer role in Runcorn, Cheshire, with travel to customer sites across the UK Ideal for Electrical, Electronic, Control & Instrumentation, Chemical, Mechatronics, Automation, Software or Telecoms Engineering graduates Working for a global leader in industrial automation, control systems and measurement technology Structured first-year programme with a route into Engineering or Technical Sales, starting in January 2027 If you’re an engineering graduate who wants to stay technical but also see how solutions are designed, priced, sold and delivered to real customers, this programme could be for you. Who’s hiring? Our client is a global name in industrial automation, with a UK business established in the 1980s. They design, deliver and support the control systems, instrumentation and technology that keep complex industrial sites running safely and efficiently. Their customers work in sectors such as energy, chemicals, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, food and drink, water and manufacturing. They’re now building the next generation of their UK team through a structured graduate programme. It’s designed to give you a complete view of the business before you choose where to specialise. What does the role look like? A first year rotating through Engineering, Proposals, Service, External Sales, Administration and QHSE (quality, health, safety and environment), so you see the full journey from customer enquiry to final solution Hands-on technical work: reviewing customer specifications and helping with system design, configuration, testing and engineering documentation Helping put together quotations, proposals and tender responses, so you learn how cost, price, risk and scope shape a winning offer Joining customer meetings, site visits and product demonstrations alongside experienced engineers and sales colleagues Support from a line manager and a mentor, with regular progress reviews and a first-year technical project Support to work towards professional registration with a relevant engineering institution At the end of year one, you and the business agree your pathway together, based on your strengths, interests and where you can add the most value Long-term routes include Systems or Application Engineer and senior specialist roles, or Technical Sales Engineer through to Account Manager, Business Development Manager or Solution Consultant What makes me right for this role? You’ll have a degree, or be expecting one, in a technical discipline such as electrical, electronic, control and instrumentation, chemical, mechatronics, automation, software or telecoms engineering. You’ll have a genuine interest in industrial automation and problem-solving. You’ll be able to think logically, pay close attention to detail and explain technical ideas clearly to people who aren’t engineers. You don’t need to know anything about their products before joining, and you don’t need sales experience. What matters is technical potential, curiosity about the commercial side, and enjoying working across different teams. An industrial placement, internship, or university design, lab or programming projects would be a bonus. You’ll need a full UK driving licence, or the ability to get one within an agreed timeframe, and you’ll need to be happy to travel to customer sites and other company locations. The selection process includes a technical reasoning exercise, a group problem-solving task, a customer scenario and a short presentation, all focused on your potential rather than polished answers. What is the package offered? · £36,000 Basic Salary · Company Bonus Applications will be managed by BMS Performance, market leading in sales recruitment.

jobs.description: Field Sales Representative – South Netherlands Products: Dental pharmaceuticals + consumables Territory: Zeeland, Limburg & Noord-Brabant We are looking for ambitious sales professionals from a dental, pharma, medical device or healthcare background. We also want to hear from experienced dental nurses, practice assistants. Treatment coordinators and practice managers who are ready to move into a commercial career. You must live in or around Eindhoven, Tilburg, Breda or ‘s-Hertogenbosch. Market-leading manufacturer with a premium product range Excellent clinical reputation and strong market share Your clinical experience is an advantage, and no commercial background is needed if you have 5+ years in a dental practice Well-performing territory with an established customer base High autonomy, with a supportive manager and no micromanagement Company car, quarterly bonus and strong earning potential THE ROLE : As Field Sales Representative, the successful candidate will manage around 1,000 accounts, roughly two thirds existing business and one third new business. This role lets you turn that knowledge into a rewarding commercial career, with a company car, a bonus and room to grow. THE COMPANY: An established, market-leading manufacturer with a great reputation in the dental sector. They provide a premium range of dental anaesthesia, pharmaceuticals and consumables, with a strong product portfolio and a customer service that is second to none. This role combines developing hospital accounts with direct patient contact, giving you the opportunity to see how the products you sell help the people using them. The role You’ll identify new business opportunities, open accounts and build relationships with key stakeholders across hospital and community services. Using clinical evidence and product demonstrations, you’ll help healthcare professionals understand the benefits of the portfolio and grow your territory. Patient contact is an important part of the role. You’ll discuss products with patients and provide practical training, working closely with an in-house patient services team that coordinates prescription requests and supply directly to patients’ homes. About you Ideally, you’ll have around two years’ relevant secondary care medical sales experience , particularly in oncology or vascular access . Your CV should demonstrate clear sales achievements and a consistent track record of developing accounts and winning business. You’ll need confidence discussing clinical information, strong relationship-building skills and an empathetic approach to patients. Knowledge of ICBs or experience with prescription-based products would be an advantage. A clinical qualification is not required. Appointment will be subject to a DBS check. Why join? With significant growth, a supportive team culture and opportunities to develop as the business expands, this is an opportunity to build your medical sales career while maintaining a direct connection with patients.

jobs.title: Medical Sales Territory Manager
jobs.location_text: South Central, South East, Thames Valley
jobs.description: Key locations: Oxford, Reading, Bracknell, Frimley and Aylesbury. A base near the M40 corridor would be ideal. A growing medical device company is doubling its sales team and looking for a Business Manager to develop its oncology and renal business across this territory. The role Working with hospital teams, including oncology services and dialysis units, you’ll open new accounts, identify key stakeholders and build lasting customer relationships. You’ll use clinical evidence and product demonstrations to explain the benefits of the portfolio and develop sales opportunities across hospital and community services. Alongside your commercial responsibilities, you’ll work directly with patients, discussing products and providing practical training. An in-house patient services team supports prescription requests and coordinates the supply of products directly to patients’ homes. About you Ideally, you’ll bring around two years’ relevant secondary care medical sales experience , particularly in oncology or vascular access , with clear achievements on your CV. You’ll be confident developing accounts, using clinical information in sales discussions and building relationships with healthcare professionals. Empathy and the ability to communicate sensitively with patients are essential. Knowledge of ICBs or experience with prescription-based products would be useful. A clinical qualification is not required, and appointment will be subject to a DBS check. Why join? You’ll join a supportive business with a strong team culture and opportunities to develop as it grows. Direct patient interaction also gives you the chance to see the benefits of the products you represent.

jobs.title: National Key Account Manager – Patient Handling
jobs.location_text: East Anglia, East Midlands, England, Home Counties, London, North East, North West, Oxon, South Central, South East, South Wales, South West, Thames Valley, West Midlands, Yorks
jobs.description: An opportunity for an experienced healthcare sales professional to take ownership of a national territory, growing an established safe patient handling portfolio across the NHS. Working with NHS Acute Trusts, Community Equipment Services and Integrated Care Systems, you’ll develop new business and expand existing accounts, helping customers improve patient care through effective equipment solutions. The role You’ll develop and deliver a nationwide growth plan, building relationships with clinical teams, procurement, operational managers, estates and senior leadership. Understanding customer priorities and navigating complex buying processes will be central to your success. Alongside supporting tenders, framework agreements and capital equipment projects, you’ll deliver product demonstrations, presentations and customer training. You’ll work closely with internal clinical and commercial colleagues to develop the right solutions for each account. About you You’ll bring a successful track record in healthcare or medical device sales into NHS acute care , with strong key account management and business development skills. Confident working with multiple stakeholders, you’ll understand how to move opportunities forward through complex sales processes. You’ll also be comfortable balancing national account planning with hands-on customer activity. This role offers scope to combine strategic account development with practical, customer-facing work in a portfolio focused on safer patient handling. To find out more about this national medical sales opportunity, contact Kirkham Young or apply with your CV for a confidential discussion.

jobs.description: Applications Specialist – Ultrasound National Role | UK | Excellent Salary & Benefits Are you an experienced Ultrasound professional who enjoys sharing your knowledge, supporting clinicians and helping others get the very best from their equipment? We’re recruiting for an Applications Specialist – Ultrasound to join a well-established medical imaging business, supporting customers across the UK. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who combines strong ultrasound knowledge with a personable, engaging approach and a genuine enthusiasm for training and developing others. You’ll be: Delivering engaging, hands-on ultrasound training to clinical teams. Supporting customers with product demonstrations, presentations and applications advice. Helping clinicians maximise the capabilities of their ultrasound systems. Building strong relationships with customers and colleagues. Working alongside the commercial team to ensure an excellent customer experience. About You We’re looking for someone who is confident, approachable and genuinely enjoys working with people. Ideally, you’ll bring: At least 2 years’ experience in ultrasound, gained in a clinical or medical device environment. Experience delivering training to healthcare professionals. Competitive salary Commission opportunity Company car or car allowance Private medical cover Employer pension contribution 26 days’ holiday plus bank holidays The opportunity to develop your career with an established medical imaging business Interested? Get in touch with Kirkham Young for a confidential conversation. We’d be delighted to tell you more. Kirkham Young | Specialist MedTech Recruitment

jobs.title: Medical Sales – Orthopaedics
jobs.location_text: Home Counties, South Central, South East, South West, Thames Valley
jobs.description: Hip & Knee | Robotics | Central South An exciting opportunity for an experienced Orthopaedic Sales Specialist to join a rapidly growing medical device company with an innovative portfolio across hip and knee reconstruction, robotic technology and tailored implant solutions . Following significant investment, the business is entering an exciting period of growth and expansion , with ambitious plans to increase its presence across the UK and further develop its innovative orthopaedic portfolio. Territory The role covers the Central South of England , with key areas including Hampshire, Wiltshire and Dorset , so you’ll ideally be based within or close to this region. The Role You’ll be responsible for developing existing business and identifying new opportunities across NHS and private hospitals throughout the territory. Working closely with orthopaedic surgeons, theatre teams and other key clinical stakeholders , you’ll support an exciting hip and knee portfolio incorporating robotic technology and tailored implant solutions designed to improve surgical outcomes and patient pathways . You’ll join an established team of four, with this opportunity arising following the retirement of a long-standing team member. What We’re Looking For Orthopaedic experience is essential for this role. Ideally, you’ll have: Proven medical device sales experience within orthopaedics Experience within hips and/or knees Strong relationships and credibility with orthopaedic surgeons and theatre teams A good understanding of NHS and private hospital sales The ability to develop existing accounts while creating new business A genuine interest in innovative surgical technology and robotics Why Consider It? This is a particularly exciting time to join the business. Significant investment is driving ambitious growth plans , creating new opportunities and supporting the continued expansion of its UK orthopaedics business. For someone who already knows the orthopaedic market and wants to work with an innovative hip, knee and robotic surgery portfolio , this is an opportunity to join a business with real momentum and play a part in its next stage of growth.
